newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa dives to two-month low as funds sell.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa dives to two-month low as funds sell.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures dived to two-month lows on Thursday in heavy volume as funds liquidated their long positions built over the recent run-up, traders said.
"It has been fund selling, trade buying all day," said one.
Another said: "The longs are wrong and are getting out."
The slide escalated as New York cocoa futures took a further tumble on speculative and fund long liquidation ahead of the long weekend.
Arbitrage selling against London was also widespread on the strength of sterling against the dollar.

Traders said the large prompt supply of cocoa in the U.S. and a perception that the El Nino weather pattern would not have any impact on the world crop until next year sparked the sell-off in New York.
The selling also came amid news of good rainfall in West Africa which could augur well for next season's crop in Ivory Coast.
LIFFE benchmark September plunged to an intraday low of 1,000 stg, the lowest since May 1 when it touched 999 stg, after triggering sell-stops at 1,050.
The contract eventually closed a hefty 89 stg down at 1,020 stg a tonne. It gapped 22 stg down at the open, and well below its previous key chart support at 1,110.
Values then managed to consolidate at between the day's range of between 1,064 and 1,087 before the lunch break.

Traders also saw the sharp reversal as a correction to the recent dazzling rally, which had hoisted prices to one-year highs. "It's a technical correction here until the new fundamental inputs are in."
This week alone, the market had lost some 14 percent in value.
Volume was heavy at 18,094 lots, centred on September contract. Options volume was meagre at 75 lots.
Traders pegged initial support at 1,000 stg after breaching the last support at the breakaway chart gap at 1,046 and 1,059 stg. Nearby resistance is seen at the previous support at 1,100.

Cocoa's frenetic run-up since mid-June was fuelled by aggressive fund-led and industry buying amid an improved chart picture and the longer-term adverse impact of the El Nino weather pattern on future harvests.
